statement: Let S be a projective K3 surface with transcendental space (T, q) of rational dimension t, put V = T(1), and let W = C+(T, q) = H1(A, Q) be an even-Clifford Kuga–Satake realization. Suppose that for one rational nonisotropic w ∈ T the tensor form of (2.4) jw : V −→ End(W), jw(v)(a) = vaw, is induced by a cycle in CH2 (S × A2)Q, using a rational polarization of W. Then, for every 1 ≤ k ≤ t, there is an injective algebraic Hodge map Fk : k ^ V −→ End(W) with an algebraic left inverse on cohomology. More precisely, put Z = A2 and n = dim Z. There are correspondences Γk ∈ CHk+1 (Sk × Z)Q, Rk ∈ CHn+k−1 (Z × Sk )Q. Viewing Vk V in H2k(Sk, Q)(k) and identifying End(W) ≃ (H1(A, Q) ⊗ H1(A, Q))(1) ⊂ H2(Z, Q)(1) by a rational polarization, their weight-zero actions satisfy (Γk)∗|∧kV = Fk and (Rk)∗Fk = id. Every rational Hodge class in Vk V is the class of a rational algebraic cycle of codimension k on Sk.
